artikel.titel: Turkey’s benign underlying inflation supports December rate cut
artikel.text: TURKEY: Turkey’s central bank raised its inflation forecast for next year to 21% from 15% previously, bringing it closer to current market expectations of 23%. Its emphasis on declining underlying inflation also points to a continuation of rate cuts in December, in our view.

artikel.titel: National Bank of Hungary preview: The door to easing is locked by external factors
artikel.text: CENTRAL AND EASTERN EUROPE: Hungary's inflation outlook remains favourable, the economy is nowhere near overheating, and the forint remains relatively stable. Local factors create room for the NBH to lower rates, but we still don’t expect any moves in the coming quarters because external risks remain elevated

artikel.titel: UK economy powers on through third quarter but the headwinds are building
artikel.text: UNITED KINGDOM: The UK economy has had a remarkable run through 2026 and as of September, there was little sign of that coming to an end. But with inflation on the rise, growth is likely to slow through the winter

artikel.titel: The Commodities Feed: Stronger dollar weighs on commodities
artikel.text: A firmer dollar and higher US yields have weighed on metals, pushing copper and gold lower. Iron ore has also weakened, while oil slipped as Middle East supply recovered

artikel.titel: FX Daily: EUR/USD gears up for a 1.10 test
artikel.text: The dollar’s strong rally this week is firmly rooted in a shift in short-term rate dynamics, driven by hawkish Fed rhetoric and hotter inflation. That makes it harder to argue for a material rebound in EUR/USD, which may instead test 1.10 should upcoming data releases offer the dollar extra support. For now, we don’t see the conditions for a break below 1.10

artikel.titel: Rates Spark: Inflation pricing sends mixed signals
artikel.text: Markets are fearful of near-term inflation risks, reinforced by this week's US CPI numbers, yet the structural outlook looks benign. We think markets risk underestimating the possibility that mounting fiscal pressures leave central banks having to tolerate higher inflation

ASIA/PACIFIC: 2026 has been a year of slowing growth and increasing divergence within China's economy. We saw the gap between external and domestic demand, as well as between the new economy and the old economy, widen significantly. Here, we look ahead to the key questions facing China in 2027

artikel.titel: Monitoring Turkey: Central bank course unchanged
artikel.text: TURKEY: October inflation interrupted the recent disinflation trend but does not appear sufficient to alter the broader policy outlook. The Central Bank of Turkey is likely to maintain its easing cycle, while geopolitical risks, reserve dynamics, and depositor behaviour remain the principal determinants of the macroeconomic trajectory

artikel.titel: Webinar: Caucasus and Central Asia outlook for 2027: resilience, ratings and risks
artikel.text: CAUCASUS AND CENTRAL ASIA: Join ING’s Dmitry Dolgin, James Wilson and Egor Fedorov on Thursday 19 November as they discuss the outlook for the Caucasus and Central Asia. The discussion will span Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, newly added to our coverage, and Uzbekistan, bringing together macro, sovereign and corporate credit perspectives. Sign up here

artikel.titel: Italian industry rebounds in September, but a recovery remains elusive
artikel.text: EUROPE: Sector performance remains uneven, with signs of improvement concentrated in capital goods. The data is consistent with the contraction in industrial value added signalled by Istat’s preliminary 3Q26 GDP release
